[YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p269#2/r2] YAHYA-SALLAM, d. 200 · قتادة | reports | Qatada says manna spoiled if kept overnight, except before the Sabbath, when Israelites gathered enough for Friday and Saturday because they did not work on the Sabbath.

[TAB-FULL:v16p126/r4] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | Both famous readings are correct: Israel was warned both that wrath would descend through disobedience and that it would become due to them.
[IBNMUJAHID:v1p421/r10] IBNMUJAHID, d. 324 · الكسائي | reports | Al-Kisāʾī alone dammas ḥāʾ in فيحل and lām in ومن يحلل; others kasra both.
[IBNMUJAHID:v1p421/r9] IBNMUJAHID, d. 324 · ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وعاصم | reports | These readers use three first-person plural forms with nūn and alif; Hamza and al-Kisāʾī use tāʾ without alif. Abu ʿAmr alone omits alif in وعدناكم throughout.
[NAHHAS:v3p52/r10] NAHHAS, d. 338 · أبو إسحاق | reports | Abu Ishaq explains “he has fallen” as having perished and reached the deepest part of Hell.
[NAHHAS:v3p52/r7] NAHHAS, d. 338 · author | holds | Abundance and well-being should not lead them to disobedience; ṭughyān means going beyond what is due.

[FARISI-HUJJA:v5p242#2/r1] FARISI-HUJJA, d. 377 · الكسائي | reports | Al-Kisāʾī alone reads both verbs with ḍamma, in yaḥullu and yaḥlil.

[MAWARDI-FULL:v3p416/r4] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | reports | A further interpretation is not to use God's provision as aid in disobeying Him.

[BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p46/r4] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · النبي | reports | A report from Ibn Masʿūd says the Qur'an came in seven aḥruf, and every verse has an outer and inner aspect, a limit, and a point of ascent; another wording gives every letter a limit and every limit an ascent. No grading is stated.

item.text: The notes cover the provision, the ban on transgression, the two verbs for wrath, and the image of falling. Some also give broader reading and interpretation principles; I’m keeping those in view so every note has a place in the map.
